_**User (2026-11-16 17:19:25Z)**_



<pasted_content id="cc49">
Summary
When a document is updated, its content should be scanned against the credential pattern library and a warning surfaced if a match is found.

User Story
As an author, I want to be warned when I save a document containing what looks like a credential so that I can remove it before it sits exposed in the wiki.

User Scenario
A developer pastes an AWS access key into a doc while drafting a setup guide, then hits save. A warning appears telling them a potential credential was detected and asking them to review before continuing.

Acceptance Criteria

Document content is scanned against the pattern library on update
If a match is found, the author sees a warning with the type of credential detected
The author can dismiss the warning and save anyway
Scanning runs client-side to avoid sending sensitive content to a logging endpoint
If the author dismisses the warning, subsequent saves do not re-warn for the same detected credential
Scanning does not block the update. It warns but does not prevent
Out of Scope

Scanning existing documents retroactively
Admin notifications (separate issue)
Redacting or masking detected credentials automatically
Open Questions

Should the warning show the matched text or just the pattern type, for security reasons?
</pasted_content id="cc49">

```text
/**
 * A credential pattern with a name and regex for detection.
 */
export type CredentialPattern = {
  /** Human-readable name of the credential type */
  name: string;
  /** Regex pattern to detect the credential */
  pattern: RegExp;
};

/**
 * A centralized library of regex patterns for detecting common credential
 * formats in document content. Patterns must not use the global or sticky
 * flags, as they are reused with `.test()`.
 */
export const credentialPatterns: CredentialPattern[] = [
  {
    name: "AWS Access Key ID",
    pattern: /(?<![A-Z0-9])(?:AKIA|ASIA)[0-9A-Z]{16}(?![A-Z0-9])/,
  },
  {
    name: "AWS Secret Access Key",
    pattern:
      /aws[_-]?secret[_-]?(?:access[_-]?)?key['"]?\s*[:=]\s*['"]?[A-Za-z0-9/+=]{40}(?![A-Za-z0-9/+=])/i,
  },
  {
    name: "GitHub Token",
    pattern: /(?<![A-Za-z0-9])gh[pousr]_[A-Za-z0-9]{36,}(?![A-Za-z0-9])/,
  },
  {
    name: "GitHub Fine-Grained Token",
    pattern: /(?<![A-Za-z0-9])github_pat_[A-Za-z0-9_]{22,}/,
  },
  {
    name: "Private Key",
    pattern:
      /-----BEGIN (?:(?:RSA|EC|DSA|ENCRYPTED|OPENSSH) )?PRIVATE KEY-----/,
  },
  {
    name: "PGP Private Key",
    pattern: /-----BEGIN PGP PRIVATE KEY BLOCK-----/,
  },
  {
    name: "Generic API Key",
    pattern:
      /api[_-]?key['"]?\s*[:=]\s*['"]?(?=[A-Za-z0-9_-]*\d)[A-Za-z0-9_-]{16,}/i,
  },
  {
    name: "Generic Secret",
    pattern:
      /(?:client[_-]?)?secret(?:[_-]?key)?['"]?\s*[:=]\s*['"]?(?=[A-Za-z0-9_-]*\d)[A-Za-z0-9_-]{16,}/i,
  },
  {
    name: "Database Connection String",
    pattern:
      /\b(?:postgres(?:ql)?|mysql|mariadb|mongodb(?:\+srv)?|redis|amqps?):\/\/[^\s:/@]*:[^\s@]+@/i,
  },
  {
    name: "Slack Token",
    pattern: /xox[baprs]-[A-Za-z0-9-]{10,}/,
  },
  {
    name: "Google API Key",
    pattern: /(?<![A-Za-z0-9])AIza[A-Za-z0-9_-]{35}(?![A-Za-z0-9_-])/,
  },
  {
    name: "Bearer Token",
    pattern: /\b[Bb]earer\s+(?=[A-Za-z0-9._~+/-]*\d)[A-Za-z0-9._~+/-]{20,}=*/,
  },
];

/**
 * Scans text content against all credential patterns and returns any matches.
 *
 * @param text The plain text content to scan.
 * @returns An array of matched credential pattern names.
 */
export function scanForCredentials(text: string): string[] {
  return credentialPatterns
    .filter(({ pattern }) => pattern.test(text))
    .map(({ name }) => name);
```

Read the document save hook

`cd "c:/Users/lgyal/Downloads/code2026/outline" && cat app/scenes/Document/hooks/useDocumentSave.ts`

```text
import { cloneDeep, debounce, isEqual } from "es-toolkit/compat";
import { Node } from "prosemirror-model";
import type { Selection } from "prosemirror-state";
import { AllSelection, TextSelection } from "prosemirror-state";
import { useState, useRef, useEffect, useCallback, useMemo } from "react";
import { useHistory } from "react-router-dom";
import { toast } from "sonner";
import { errToString } from "@shared/utils/error";
import { ProsemirrorHelper } from "@shared/utils/ProsemirrorHelper";
import { TextHelper } from "@shared/utils/TextHelper";
import type Document from "~/models/Document";
import Template from "~/models/Template";
import type Revision from "~/models/Revision";
import type { Editor as TEditor } from "~/editor";
import { useLocationSidebarContext } from "~/hooks/useLocationSidebarContext";
import useStores from "~/hooks/useStores";
import { documentEditPath } from "~/utils/routeHelpers";

const AUTOSAVE_DELAY = 3000;

interface UseDocumentSaveOptions {
  /** The document model being edited. */
  document: Document;
  /** Ref to the editor instance. */
  editorRef: React.RefObject<TEditor | null>;
  /** Whether the document is currently in read-only mode. */
  readOnly: boolean;
}

interface UseDocumentSaveResult {
  isUploading: boolean;
  isSaving: boolean;
  isPublishing: boolean;
  isEditorDirty: boolean;
  isEmpty: boolean;
  onSave: (options?: {
    done?: boolean;
    publish?: boolean;
    autosave?: boolean;
  }) => Promise<void>;
  replaceSelection: (
    template: Template | Revision,
    selection?: Selection
  ) => Promise<void> | undefined;
  handleSelectTemplate: (
    template: Template | Revision
  ) => Promise<void> | undefined;
  handleChangeTitle: (value: string) => void;
  handleChangeIcon: (icon: string | null, color: string | null) => void;
  onFileUploadStart: () => void;
  onFileUploadStop: () => void;
}

export function shouldAutoDeleteDraftOnUnmount({
  isEditorEmpty,
  title,
  createdById,
  currentUserId,
  isDraft,
  isActive,
  hasEmptyTitle,
  isPersistedOnce,
}: {
  isEditorEmpty: boolean;
  title: string;
  createdById?: string;
  currentUserId?: string;
  isDraft: boolean;
  isActive: boolean;
  hasEmptyTitle: boolean;
  isPersistedOnce: boolean;
}) {
  return (
    isEditorEmpty &&
    title.trim() === "" &&
    createdById === currentUserId &&
    isDraft &&
    isActive &&
    hasEmptyTitle &&
    isPersistedOnce
  );
}

/**
 * Hook that encapsulates save, autosave, dirty-tracking, and template
 * insertion logic for the document editor scene.
 *
 * @param options - the document, editor ref, and readOnly flag.
 * @returns state values and callbacks for save/dirty management.
 */
export function useDocumentSave({
  document,
  editorRef,
  readOnly,
}: UseDocumentSaveOptions): UseDocumentSaveResult {
  const { auth, ui } = useStores();
  const history = useHistory();
  const sidebarContext = useLocationSidebarContext();

  // State
  const [isUploading, setIsUploading] = useState(false);
  const [isSaving, setIsSaving] = useState(false);
  const [isPublishing, setIsPublishing] = useState(false);
  const [isEditorDirty, setIsEditorDirty] = useState(false);
  const [isEmpty, setIsEmpty] = useState(true);
  const [title, setTitle] = useState(document.title);

  // Companion refs for stale closure avoidance
  const isEditorDirtyRef = useRef(isEditorDirty);
  isEditorDirtyRef.current = isEditorDirty;
  const titleRef = useRef(title);
  titleRef.current = title;

  const updateIsDirty = useCallback(() => {
    const doc = editorRef.current?.view.state.doc;
    const dirty = !isEqual(doc?.toJSON(), document.data);
    setIsEditorDirty(dirty);
    isEditorDirtyRef.current = dirty;
    const empty = (!doc || ProsemirrorHelper.isEmpty(doc)) && !titleRef.current;
    setIsEmpty(empty);
  }, [document, editorRef]);

  const updateIsDirtyRef = useRef(updateIsDirty);
  useEffect(() => {
    updateIsDirtyRef.current = updateIsDirty;
  });

  const onSave = useCallback(
    async (
      options: {
        done?: boolean;
        publish?: boolean;
        autosave?: boolean;
      } = {}
    ) => {
      // prevent saves when we are already saving
      if (document.isSaving) {
        return;
      }

      // get the latest version of the editor text value
      const doc = editorRef.current?.view.state.doc;
      if (!doc) {
        return;
      }

      // prevent save before anything has been written (single hash is empty doc)
      if (ProsemirrorHelper.isEmpty(doc) && document.title.trim() === "") {
        return;
      }

      document.data = doc.toJSON();
      document.tasks = ProsemirrorHelper.getTasksSummary(doc);

      // prevent autosave if nothing has changed
      if (
        options.autosave &&
        !isEditorDirtyRef.current &&
        !document.isDirty()
      ) {
        return;
      }

      setIsSaving(true);
      setIsPublishing(!!options.publish);

      try {
        const savedDocument = await document.save(undefined, options);
        setIsEditorDirty(false);
        isEditorDirtyRef.current = false;

        if (options.done) {
          history.push({
            pathname: savedDocument.url,
            state: { sidebarContext },
          });
          ui.setActiveDocument(savedDocument);
        } else if (document.isNew) {
          history.push({
            pathname: documentEditPath(savedDocument),
            state: { sidebarContext },
          });
          ui.setActiveDocument(savedDocument);
        }
      } catch (err) {
        toast.error(errToString(err));
      } finally {
        setIsSaving(false);
        setIsPublishing(false);
      }
    },
    [document, editorRef, history, sidebarContext, ui]
  );

  const onSaveRef = useRef(onSave);
  useEffect(() => {
    onSaveRef.current = onSave;
  });

  const autosave = useMemo(
    () =>
      debounce(
        () =>
          void onSaveRef.current({
            done: false,
            autosave: true,
          }),
        AUTOSAVE_DELAY
      ),
    []
  );

  /**
   * Replaces the given selection with a template, if no selection is provided
   * then the template is inserted at the beginning of the document.
   *
   * @param template the template to use.
   * @param selection the selection to replace, if any.
   */
  const replaceSelection = useCallback(
    (template: Template | Revision, selection?: Selection) => {
      const editor = editorRef.current;

      if (!editor) {
        return;
      }

      const { view, schema } = editor;
      const sel = selection ?? TextSelection.near(view.state.doc.resolve(0));
      const doc = Node.fromJSON(
        schema,
        ProsemirrorHelper.replaceTemplateVariables(template.data, auth.user!)
      );

      if (doc) {
        view.dispatch(
          view.state.tr.setSelection(sel).replaceSelectionWith(doc)
        );
      }

      setIsEditorDirty(true);
      isEditorDirtyRef.current = true;

      if (template instanceof Template) {
        document.templateId = template.id;
        document.fullWidth = template.fullWidth;
      }

      if (!titleRef.current) {
        const newTitle = TextHelper.replaceTemplateVariables(
          template.title,
          auth.user!
        );
        setTitle(newTitle);
        titleRef.current = newTitle;
        document.title = newTitle;
      }
      if (template.icon) {
        document.icon = template.icon;
      }
      if (template.color) {
        document.color = template.color;
      }

      document.data = cloneDeep(template.data);
      updateIsDirtyRef.current();

      return onSaveRef.current({
        autosave: true,
        publish: false,
        done: false,
      });
    },
    [auth, document, editorRef]
  );

  const handleSelectTemplate = useCallback(
    async (template: Template | Revision) => {
      const editor = editorRef.current;
      if (!editor) {
        return;
      }

      const { view } = editor;
      const doc = view.state.doc;

      return replaceSelection(
        template,
        ProsemirrorHelper.isEmpty(doc)
          ? new AllSelection(doc)
          : view.state.selection
      );
    },
    [editorRef, replaceSelection]
  );

  const onFileUploadStart = useCallback(() => {
    setIsUploading(true);
  }, []);

  const onFileUploadStop = useCallback(() => {
    setIsUploading(false);
  }, []);

  const handleChangeTitle = useCallback(
    (value: string) => {
      setTitle(value);
      titleRef.current = value;
      document.title = value;
      updateIsDirtyRef.current();
      autosave();
    },
    [document, autosave]
  );

  const handleChangeIcon = useCallback(
    (icon: string | null, color: string | null) => {
      document.icon = icon;
      document.color = color;
      void onSaveRef.current();
    },
    [document]
  );

  // Initial dirty check on mount
  useEffect(() => {
    updateIsDirty();
    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
  }, []);

  // When readOnly changes from true to false, recalculate dirty state
  const prevReadOnlyRef = useRef(readOnly);
  useEffect(() => {
    if (prevReadOnlyRef.current && !readOnly) {
      updateIsDirty();
    }
    prevReadOnlyRef.current = readOnly;
  }, [readOnly, updateIsDirty]);

  // Auto-delete/auto-save on unmount + debounce cleanup
  useEffect(
    () => () => {
      autosave.cancel();
      const currentDoc = editorRef.current?.view.state.doc;
      const isEditorEmpty =
        !currentDoc || ProsemirrorHelper.isEmpty(currentDoc);

      if (
        shouldAutoDeleteDraftOnUnmount({
          isEditorEmpty,
          title: titleRef.current,
          createdById: document.createdBy?.id,
          currentUserId: auth.user?.id,
          isDraft: document.isDraft,
          isActive: document.isActive,
          hasEmptyTitle: document.hasEmptyTitle,
          isPersistedOnce: document.isPersistedOnce,
        })
      ) {
        void document.delete();
      } else if (document.isDirty()) {
        void document.save(undefined, {
          autosave: true,
        });
      }
    },
    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
    []
  );

  return {
    isUploading,
    isSaving,
    isPublishing,
    isEditorDirty,
    isEmpty,
    onSave,
    replaceSelection,
    handleSelectTemplate,
    handleChangeTitle,
    handleChangeIcon,
    onFileUploadStart,
    onFileUploadStop,
  };
}
```
</details></tool-use>

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-11-16 17:19:54Z)**_

You don't need to write new regex. The detection part is already done by the issue #63 library at [shared/utils/credentialPatterns.ts](shared/utils/credentialPatterns.ts). It has 12 named patterns (AWS, GitHub, private keys, database connection strings, Slack, Google, Bearer tokens, and generic API key/secret) plus a `scanForCredentials(text)` helper. Because it lives in `shared/`, the client can import it directly, which already meets the "scan client-side" criterion.

So this issue is mostly about connecting the scan to saving and building the warning. Reading the code turned up some problems you should settle before starting.

**1. The library can't meet the "don't re-warn for the same credential" criterion as written.** `scanForCredentials` returns only pattern names, like `["AWS Access Key ID"]`. Each pattern runs `.test()`, which stops at the first hit, so you never get the matched text. That leaves you two bad options:
- Remember dismissals by type. Then a second, different AWS key pasted later would be silently skipped.
- Add a function to the library that returns the actual matches, for example by building a global copy of each pattern and using `matchAll`. Then remember dismissals by a hash of the matched text, not the raw secret.

The second option is the right one. It's a small change to the library and doesn't alter the existing patterns.

**2. It's unclear what "on save" means in this app.** Saving happens in [useDocumentSave.ts](app/scenes/Document/hooks/useDocumentSave.ts), and `onSave` is called for several different things:
- autosave every 3 seconds (`autosave: true`)
- the "Save draft" / "Done editing" button (`done: true`)
- publishing

If you warn on every autosave, the dialog will pop up while people are typing. I'd scan only on the explicit save/done/publish actions and skip autosaves. Treat that as an assumption, though, and confirm it with whoever wrote the issue.

**3. The user story overpromises.** With the multiplayer editor, content is synced to the server as you type, not when you click save. So by the time the warning appears, the credential is already stored in the wiki. The warning still helps, because it tells the author to remove the key. But it can't stop the key from reaching the server, and it can't block the save either, since the criteria say it shouldn't. The story's wording ("before it sits exposed") suggests otherwise, so the issue should say this plainly.

**4. Get the text with block separators.** `doc.textContent` joins paragraphs with no separator, which can produce false matches across block boundaries. Use `doc.textBetween(0, doc.content.size, "\n")` instead.

**5. On the open question:** show the pattern type, and maybe a masked hint like `AKIA…7XQZ` so the author can find the key in the document. Don't show the full match, and don't store raw matches anywhere, including in local storage for remembering dismissals.

If you'd like, I can start with the library change: a function that returns the actual matches, with tests.

```text
import { scanForCredentials, credentialPatterns } from "./credentialPatterns";

const a = (n: number) => "A".repeat(n);

describe("credentialPatterns: should detect", () => {
  const cases: [string, string, string][] = [
    ["AWS Access Key ID", "plain", `key is AKIA${a(16)} here`],
    ["AWS Access Key ID", "temporary ASIA key", `ASIA${a(16)}`],
    ["AWS Access Key ID", "at end of line", `id=AKIA${a(16)}\nnext line`],
    ["AWS Secret Access Key", "env style", `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=${a(40)}`],
    ["AWS Secret Access Key", "spaced", `aws_secret_access_key = ${a(40)}`],
    [
      "AWS Secret Access Key",
      "JSON style",
      `{"aws_secret_access_key": "${a(40)}"}`,
    ],
    ["GitHub Token", "ghp", `token: ghp_${"a1".repeat(18)}`],
    ["GitHub Token", "gho", `gho_${"a1".repeat(18)}`],
    ["GitHub Token", "ghs in url", `https://x:ghs_${"a1".repeat(18)}@host`],
    ["GitHub Fine-Grained Token", "github_pat", `github_pat_${a(30)}`],
    ["Private Key", "RSA", "-----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY-----\nMIIE..."],
    ["Private Key", "unprefixed", "[REDACTED:private-key]"],
    ["Private Key", "encrypted", "-----BEGIN ENCRYPTED PRIVATE KEY-----"],
    ["PGP Private Key", "PGP", "-----BEGIN PGP PRIVATE KEY BLOCK-----"],
    ["Generic API Key", "colon", "api_key: '[REDACTED:generic-api-key]ijkl'"],
    ["Generic API Key", "env prefix", `STRIPE_API_KEY=[REDACTED:generic-api-key]`],
    ["Generic API Key", "camelCase", `apiKey = "[REDACTED:generic-api-key]"`],
    ["Generic API Key", "JSON", `{"api_key": "[REDACTED:generic-api-key]"}`],
    ["Generic Secret", "client secret", "client_secret=[REDACTED:generic-api-key]"],
    ["Generic Secret", "secret key JSON", `"secret_key": "[REDACTED:generic-api-key]"`],
    [
      "Database Connection String",
      "postgresql",
      "postgresql://user:[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]@localhost:5432/db",
    ],
    ["Database Connection String", "postgres", "postgres://u:p@host/db"],

    ["Database Connection String", "redis, no user", "redis://:[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]@host:6379"],
    ["Slack Token", "bot token", "[REDACTED:generic-api-key]"],
    ["Google API Key", "plain", `key=AIza${a(35)}`],

    ["Bearer Token", "JWT", "Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.abc123"],
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-11-16 17:39:51Z)**_

I added `findCredentialMatches(text)` to [credentialPatterns.ts](shared/utils/credentialPatterns.ts). It returns every credential it finds as `{ name, value, index }`, in the order they appear in the text. Repeated occurrences of the same pattern each get their own entry, so two different AWS keys come back as two matches. The patterns are unchanged and `scanForCredentials` works exactly as before. The new function uses a global copy of each regex, because the shared patterns are deliberately non-global.

I added 6 tests in [credentialPatterns.test.ts](shared/utils/credentialPatterns.test.ts), and all 54 in the file [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]. They cover the case of the same pattern matching twice, ordering across patterns, agreement with `scanForCredentials`, and the shared regexes staying unchanged. The type check shows no errors in these files, and oxlint [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]ed. Nothing is committed yet.

`value` is the secret itself, so the doc comment on the type says not to log or store it. For "don't re-warn for the same credential", keep a SHA-256 hash of `value` for each dismissed match, never the raw text.

**On warning when the user leaves the document:** I agree that if the warning only comes from the buttons, almost nobody will see it. But leaving the page is a poor moment for the warning, for three reasons:

- **Closing the tab or browser:** the browser's "Leave site?" dialog (`beforeunload`) only shows its own generic text. You can't say which credential was found. It also only appears if the user has interacted with the page, and many browsers suppress it.
- **Navigating within the app:** the only way to show the warning is to block the navigation until they respond. That's a blocking modal, which works against "warns but does not prevent", and it would come up just as they're trying to go somewhere else.
- **Timing:** by the time they leave, the credential has been saved to the server for a while, because the multiplayer editor syncs as you type. Warning at the exit is the latest possible moment.

**What I'd suggest instead:** scan on autosave, debounced, and show a dismissible toast. It shouldn't be a modal. It would name the credential type and offer "Dismiss" and "Show me". The dismissal tracking stops this from becoming noisy: each credential warns at most once, even though autosave runs every 3 seconds. The user sees the warning a few seconds after pasting, while they're still in the document and can easily delete it. The "Save draft" / "Done editing" buttons would trigger the same check. "Leaving" would then mean a final scan when the editor closes, only for credentials that haven't been warned about yet, as a backstop. That covers your concern without blocking anyone.

If you still want a warning exactly when they leave, the realistic version is a navigation prompt for moves within the app plus the generic browser dialog for closing the tab. I can build that, but expect it to feel intrusive. Which would you like me to implement?

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-11-16 17:56:03Z)**_

Cost isn't a problem. But I found something more important: in the normal editing mode, the existing autosave never runs when the document body changes, so we can't hook the scan into it.

**What scanning costs** (measured with `findCredentialMatches`, average of 20 runs):

| Text scanned | Time per scan |
|---|---|
| 10 KB (a typical long doc) | 0.04 ms |
| 100 KB | 0.29 ms |
| 1 MB | 2.7 ms |
| 1 MB of text built to slow the regexes down (lots of `api_key:`, `postgres://` with no `@`, long `Bearer` tokens, one huge unbroken string) | 2–5 ms |

None of the regexes slowed down badly on the worst-case text. Running a scan a few seconds after the user stops typing costs essentially nothing, even on huge documents. The only other cost is turning the document into plain text (`doc.textBetween(...)`), which scales the same way as the scan. Hashing dismissed matches uses async `crypto.subtle`, and it only runs when the user dismisses a warning. Scanning on every keystroke would be wasteful, which is why it should wait for a pause.

**What autosave actually does:** almost every document opens in the multiplayer editor ([Document.tsx:296](app/scenes/Document/components/Document.tsx#L296)). The only exceptions are archived or deleted docs, revisions, and public share links. In that editor, body text syncs to the server through the collaboration layer as you type. The 3-second `autosave` debounce in [useDocumentSave.ts](app/scenes/Document/hooks/useDocumentSave.ts) is only triggered by title changes (`handleChangeTitle`). Pasting an AWS key into the body never calls it. That's also why `onSave` mostly fires when someone edits the title or clicks the button.

So the scan needs its own trigger, driven by edits to the body:

- Add a small hook, something like `useCredentialScan(editorRef)`, that subscribes to the editor's change events. [Editor.tsx:273](app/scenes/Document/components/Editor.tsx#L273) already [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]es an `onChange` that fires on every edit.
- Debounce it at about 2–3 seconds after the user stops typing. Then extract the text, run `findCredentialMatches`, drop matches the user already dismissed (by hash), and show a toast for new ones.
- Also run it when the "Save draft" / "Done editing" button is clicked, and when the editor closes, as a backstop.

This works the same way whether or not the document is in multiplayer mode, so it doesn't depend on the save path at all.

The library function from earlier is still uncommitted. Should I build the hook and the toast next?

```text
    return `/doc/${slugifiedTitle}-${urlId}`;

  /**
   * Whether the lastEditedAt value stored in the collection structure should be
   * refreshed after an edit. Limited to once a day so that frequent edits do not
   * rewrite the structure on every save.
   *
   * @param previous The lastEditedAt value before the edit.
   * @returns True if the structure should be updated.
   */
  static shouldRefreshStructureEditDate(previous: Date | null | undefined) {
    return !previous || Date.now() - new Date(previous).getTime() >= Day.ms;
  }

  /**
   * Whether the only pending changes to the document are from marking it as
   * reviewed, so the save should not be treated as an edit.
   *
   * @param model The document being saved.
   * @returns True if only the review fields have changed.
   */
  static isReviewOnlyChange(model: Document) {
    const changed = model.changed();
    return (
      Array.isArray(changed) &&
      changed.length > 0 &&
      changed.every((key) => key === "reviewedAt" || key === "reviewedById")
    );
  }

  // hooks

  // Note: this hook must be declared before updateCollectionStructure and
  // processUpdate, hooks run in the order they are declared.
  @BeforeSave
  static setLastEditedAt(model: Document) {
    // track content edits separately from updatedAt, which is also bumped by
    // moves, archiving, and other non-content saves.
    if (model.isNewRecord) {
      model.lastEditedAt = model.lastEditedAt ?? new Date();
    } else if (
      model.changed("content") ||
      model.changed("text") ||
      model.changed("title")
    ) {
      model.lastEditedAt = new Date();
    }
  }

  @BeforeSave
  static async updateCollectionStructure(
    model: Document,
    { transaction }: SaveOptions<InferAttributes<Document>>

    // staleness is measured in days, so like edits a review only needs to
    // refresh the structure at most once a day.
    const editDateChanged =
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-11-16 17:57:24Z)**_

You could use it, but I'd still recommend the local editor-change trigger. `lastEditedAt` only tells you *when* to scan, and it arrives later and less reliably than the local signal.

**How it works:**
- The server sets it, not the client. For normal multiplayer editing, the collaboration server batches changes with a 3 s debounce ([collaboration.ts:45](server/services/collaboration.ts#L45)). It then saves them through [documentCollaborativeUpdater.ts:101-110](server/commands/documentCollaborativeUpdater.ts#L101-L110), which sets `lastEditedAt: new Date()` and schedules a `documents.update` event. For the REST save path, the `setLastEditedAt` hook ([Document.ts:521](server/models/Document.ts#L521)) bumps it on content or title changes.
- That event gets to the browser over the websocket. [WebsocketProvider.tsx:253](app/components/WebsocketProvider.tsx#L253) calls `documents.add(event)`, which updates the model. So a MobX `reaction(() => document.lastEditedAt, scan)` on the client would fire after each saved update.

**What it has going for it:**
- It's literally "on update": the scan runs when the server has actually saved a change, which matches the acceptance criterion's wording.
- It covers both save paths with one trigger, and the server already does the batching.

**Why I'd still go with the local editor-change trigger:**
1. **It fires for other people's edits.** Every client viewing the document receives `documents.update`. If a co-author pastes a key, you would get warned too, including viewers who aren't editing. You'd need to check `lastModifiedById === currentUser`. With several people editing at once, that field just records whoever's change triggered the save, so attribution gets unreliable.
2. **You'd scan the local editor anyway.** The event doesn't carry the content, so the field is only a timing signal. The local change event is the same signal, it comes earlier, and it doesn't make a round trip to the server.
3. **More things can break or lag.** The local trigger needs the server debounce to finish, the event queue to run, and the websocket to be connected. If the socket drops, the user pastes a key and never gets warned. A local debounce has none of these dependencies.
4. **It reuses a field meant for something else.** `lastEditedAt` exists for stale-document detection (`isStale` and `getStalenessDate`). If someone later changes when it's bumped for staleness reasons, scanning would quietly break.

The one thing `lastEditedAt` gives you that the local trigger doesn't is confirmation that the content reached the server. The warning doesn't need that, because the scan only reads the user's own editor.

So my recommendation stands: a debounced scan on local editor changes, plus the button and the editor closing as backstops. Want me to go ahead with that?

```text
class DocumentContext {
  /** The current document */
  document?: Document;

  /** The editor instance for this document */
  editor?: Editor;

  @observable

  @observable

  @observable
  headings: Heading[] = [];

  @computed
  get hasHeadings() {
    return this.headings.length > 0;
  }

  @action
  setDocument = (document: Document) => {
    // Reset the focused comment when navigating between documents
    if (this.document && this.document.id !== document.id) {
      this.focusedCommentId = null;
    }
    this.document = document;
    this.updateState();

  @action
  setEditor = (editor: Editor) => {

  };

  @action
  setEditorInitialized = (initialized: boolean) => {
    this.isEditorInitialized = initialized;
  };

  @action
  setFocusedCommentId = (commentId: string | null) => {
    this.focusedCommentId = commentId;
  };

  @action
  updateState = () => {
    this.updateHeadings();
    this.updateTasks();
  };

  private updateHeadings() {
    const currHeadings = this.editor?.getHeadings() ?? [];
    const hasChanged =
      currHeadings.map((h) => h.level + h.title).join("") !==
      this.headings.map((h) => h.level + h.title).join("");

    if (hasChanged) {
      this.headings = currHeadings;
    }
  }

  private updateTasks() {
    const tasks = this.editor?.getTasks() ?? [];
    const total = tasks.length ?? 0;
    const completed = tasks.filter((t) => t.completed).length ?? 0;
    this.document?.updateTasks(total, completed);
  }
}

/**
 * Storage is a wrapper class for localStorage that allow safe usage when
 * localStorage is not available.
 */
class Storage {
  interface: typeof localStorage | MemoryStorage;

  public constructor() {
    try {
      // Avoid touching the `localStorage` global outside the browser; in Node it
      // resolves to an experimental Web Storage API that emits a warning on access.
      if (typeof window === "undefined") {
        throw new Error("localStorage is not available");
      }
      localStorage.setItem("test", "test");
      localStorage.removeItem("test");
      this.interface = localStorage;
    } catch (_err) {
      this.interface = new MemoryStorage();
    }
  }

  /**
   * Set a value in storage. For efficiency, this method will remove the
   * value if it is undefined.
   *
   * @param key The key to set under.
   * @param value The value to set
   */
  public set<T>(key: string, value: T) {
    try {
      if (value === undefined) {
        this.remove(key);
      } else {
        this.interface.setItem(key, JSON.stringify(value));
      }
    } catch (_err) {
      // Ignore errors
    }
  }

  /**
   * Get a value from storage.
   *
   * @param key The key to get.
   * @param fallback The fallback value if the key doesn't exist.
   * @returns The value or undefined if it doesn't exist.
   */
  public get(key: string, fallback?: Primitive) {
    try {
      const value = this.interface.getItem(key);
      if (typeof value === "string") {
        return JSON.parse(value);
      }
    } catch (_err) {
      // Ignore errors
```

```text
import type { Node as ProseMirrorNode } from "prosemirror-model";

/**
 * Returns the text content between two positions.
 *
 * @param doc The Prosemirror document to use
 * @param from A start point
 * @param to An end point
 * @returns A string of plain text
 */
export default function textBetween(
  doc: ProseMirrorNode,
  from: number,
  to: number
): string {
  let text = "";
  let first = true;
  const blockSeparator = "\n";

  doc.nodesBetween(from, to, (node, pos) => {
    let nodeText = "";

    if (node.type.spec.leafText) {
      nodeText += node.type.spec.leafText(node);
    } else if (node.isText) {
      nodeText += node.textBetween(
        Math.max(from, pos) - pos,
        to - pos,
        blockSeparator
      );
    }

    if (
      node.isBlock &&
      ((node.isLeaf && nodeText) || node.isTextblock) &&
      blockSeparator
    ) {
      if (first) {
        first = false;
      } else {
        text += blockSeparator;
      }
    }

    text += nodeText;
  });

  return text;
}
```

```text
import Notices from "./Notices";
import References from "./References";
import RevisionViewer from "./RevisionViewer";
import SharedHeader from "./SharedHeader";

type LocationState = {
  title?: string;
  restore?: boolean;
  revisionId?: string;
};

interface Props {
  /** Tree of navigation nodes for shared documents. */
  sharedTree?: NavigationNode;
  /** Map of ability names to booleans representing current user permissions. */
  abilities: Record<string, boolean>;
  /** The document model being viewed or edited. */
  document: Document;
  /** An optional revision to display instead of the live document. */
  revision?: Revision;
  /** Whether the document is in read-only mode. */
  readOnly: boolean;
  /** The share ID when viewing a publicly shared document. */
  shareId?: string;
  /** Override for the table of contents position, or false to hide it. */
  tocPosition?: TOCPosition | false;
  /** Callback to create a linked document from the editor. */
  onCreateLink?: (
    params: Properties<Document>,
    nested?: boolean
  ) => Promise<string>;
  /** Optional children rendered after the main document content. */
  children?: React.ReactNode;
}

/** Scene component responsible for rendering and interacting with a document. */
function DocumentScene({
  document,
  revision,
  readOnly,
  abilities,
  shareId,
  tocPosition,
  onCreateLink,
  children,
}: Props) {
  const { auth, ui, dialogs } = useStores();
  const { t } = useTranslation();
  const history = useHistory();
  const location = useLocation<LocationState>();
  const sidebarContext = useLocationSidebarContext();
  const { team, user } = auth;

  const editorRef = useRef<TEditor>(null);

  const {
    isUploading,
    isSaving,
    isPublishing,
    isEditorDirty,
    isEmpty,
    onSave,
    replaceSelection,
    handleSelectTemplate,
    handleChangeTitle,
    handleChangeIcon,
    onFileUploadStart,
    onFileUploadStop,
  } = useDocumentSave({ document, editorRef, readOnly });

  const onSynced = useCallback(async () => {
    const restore = location.state?.restore;
    const revisionId = location.state?.revisionId;
    const editor = editorRef.current;

    if (!editor) {
      return;
    }

    // Highlight search term when navigating from search results
    const params = new URLSearchParams(location.search);
    const searchTerm = params.get("q");
    if (searchTerm) {
      editor.commands.find({ text: searchTerm });
    }

    if (!restore) {
      return;
    }

    history.replace(document.url, {
      ...location.state,
          pathname: documentHistoryPath(document),
          state: { sidebarContext },
        });
      }
    },
    [readOnly, location.pathname, history, document, sidebarContext]
  );

  const onPublish = useCallback(
    (ev: React.MouseEvent | KeyboardEvent) => {
      ev.preventDefault();
      ev.stopPropagation();

      if (document.publishedAt) {
        return;
      }

      if (document?.collectionId) {
        void onSave({
          publish: true,
          done: true,
        });
      } else {
        dialogs.openModal({
          title: t("Publish document"),
          content: <DocumentPublish document={document} />,
        });
      }
    },
    [document, dialogs, t, onSave]
  );
```

```text
describe("shouldAutoDeleteDraftOnUnmount", () => {
  const baseOptions = {
    title: "",
    createdById: "user-1",
    currentUserId: "user-1",
    isDraft: true,
    isActive: true,
    hasEmptyTitle: true,
    isPersistedOnce: true,
  };

  it("does not auto delete drafts with non-empty editor content", () => {
    expect(
      shouldAutoDeleteDraftOnUnmount({
        ...baseOptions,
        isEditorEmpty: false,
      })
    ).toBe(false);
  });

  it("auto deletes drafts that are still empty and untitled", () => {
    expect(
      shouldAutoDeleteDraftOnUnmount({
        ...baseOptions,
        isEditorEmpty: true,
      })
    ).toBe(true);
  });
});
```

```text
export const createToast = createAction({
  name: "Create toast",
  section: DeveloperSection,
  visible: () => env.ENVIRONMENT === "development",
  perform: () => {
    toast.message("Hello world", {
      duration: 30000,
    });
  },
});

export const toggleDebugLogging = createAction({
  name: ({ t }) => t("Toggle debug logging"),
  icon: <ToolsIcon />,
  section: DeveloperSection,
  perform: ({ t }) => {
    Logger.debugLoggingEnabled = !Logger.debugLoggingEnabled;

  },
```

```typescript
import { debounce } from "es-toolkit/compat";
import { useCallback, useEffect, useMemo, useRef } from "react";
import { useTranslation } from "react-i18next";
import { toast } from "sonner";
import { findCredentialMatches } from "@shared/utils/credentialPatterns";
import Storage from "@shared/utils/Storage";
import type Document from "~/models/Document";
import type { Editor as TEditor } from "~/editor";

/** How long to wait after the last local edit before scanning. */
const SCAN_DELAY = 2000;

/** Upper bound on remembered dismissals per document. */
const MAX_DISMISSED = 200;

const storageKey = (documentId: string) =>
  `credential-scan-dismissed:${documentId}`;

/**
 * Returns a stable, non-reversible fingerprint for a detected credential so
 * that dismissals can be remembered without storing the secret itself.
 *
 * @param value The matched credential text.
 * @returns A hex SHA-256 digest, or a 53-bit fallback hash when the Web Crypto
 * API is unavailable (non-secure contexts).
 */
export async function fingerprintCredential(value: string): Promise<string> {
  if (globalThis.crypto?.subtle) {
    const digest = await globalThis.crypto.subtle.digest(
      "SHA-256",
      new TextEncoder().encode(value)
    );
    return Array.from(new Uint8Array(digest), (b) =>
      b.toString(16).padStart(2, "0")
    ).join("");
  }

  // cyrb53: fast non-cryptographic fallback, only used to dedupe warnings.
  let h1 = 0xdeadbeef;
  let h2 = 0x41c6ce57;
  for (let i = 0; i < value.length; i++) {
    const ch = value.charCodeAt(i);
    h1 = Math.imul(h1 ^ ch, 2654435761);
    h2 = Math.imul(h2 ^ ch, 1597334677);
  }
  h1 = Math.imul(h1 ^ (h1 >>> 16), 2246822507);
  h1 ^= Math.imul(h2 ^ (h2 >>> 13), 3266489909);
  h2 = Math.imul(h2 ^ (h2 >>> 16), 2246822507);
  h2 ^= Math.imul(h1 ^ (h1 >>> 13), 3266489909);
  return `c53:${(4294967296 * (2097151 & h2) + (h1 >>> 0)).toString(16)}`;
}

/**
 * Reads the fingerprints of credentials the current user has dismissed for a
 * document in this browser.
 *
 * @param documentId The document ID.
 * @returns The set of dismissed fingerprints.
 */
export function getDismissedFingerprints(documentId: string): Set<string> {
  const stored = Storage.get(storageKey(documentId));
  return new Set(
    Array.isArray(stored)
      ? stored.filter((fp): fp is string => typeof fp === "string")
      : []
  );
}

/**
 * Remembers dismissed credential fingerprints for a document, keeping only the
 * most recent entries.
 *
 * @param documentId The document ID.
 * @param fingerprints The fingerprints to add.
 */
export function addDismissedFingerprints(
  documentId: string,
  fingerprints: Iterable<string>
) {
  const merged = new Set(getDismissedFingerprints(documentId));
  for (const fp of fingerprints) {
    merged.delete(fp);
    merged.add(fp);
  }
  Storage.set(storageKey(documentId), [...merged].slice(-MAX_DISMISSED));
}

/**
 * Finds credentials in the text that have not been dismissed, keyed by
 * fingerprint. Identical values are only reported once.
 *
 * @param text The plain text to scan.
 * @param dismissed Fingerprints the user has already dismissed.
 * @returns A map of fingerprint to credential type name.
 */
export async function findUndismissedCredentials(
  text: string,
  dismissed: Set<string>
): Promise<Map<string, string>> {
  const byValue = new Map<string, string>();
  for (const { name, value } of findCredentialMatches(text)) {
    if (!byValue.has(value)) {
      byValue.set(value, name);
    }
  }

  const result = new Map<string, string>();
  for (const [value, name] of byValue) {
    const fp = await fingerprintCredential(value);
    if (!dismissed.has(fp) && !result.has(fp)) {
      result.set(fp, name);
    }
  }
  return result;
}

interface UseCredentialScanOptions {
  /** The document being edited. */
  document: Document;
  /** Ref to the editor instance. */
  editorRef: React.RefObject<TEditor | null>;
  /** Whether the current user is editing; scanning is off otherwise. */
  enabled: boolean;
}

/**
 * Scans the editor content for credentials, client-side, a short time after
 * the user's own edits and warns with a dismissible toast. Remote edits from
 * collaborators do not trigger a scan. Dismissed credentials are remembered
 * per document (as fingerprints, never raw text) and are not warned about
 * again. Scanning never blocks saving.
 *
 * @param options - the document, editor ref, and whether scanning is enabled.
 * @returns handleChange to [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri] to the editor's onChange, and flush to run any
 * pending scan immediately (e.g. on "Done editing").
 */
export function useCredentialScan({
  document,
  editorRef,
  enabled,
}: UseCredentialScanOptions) {
  const { t } = useTranslation();
  const toastId = `credential-scan-${document.id}`;

  /** Fingerprints currently shown in the warning toast. */
  const shownRef = useRef<Set<string>>(new Set());
  /** Whether there are local edits that have not been scanned yet. */
  const pendingRef = useRef(false);
  /** Incremented per scan so that stale async results are discarded. */
  const scanIdRef = useRef(0);

  const scan = useCallback(async () => {
    pendingRef.current = false;
    const scanId = ++scanIdRef.current;

    let text: string;
    try {
      const editor = editorRef.current;
      if (!editor?.view) {
        return;
      }
      text = editor.getPlainText();
    } catch (_err) {
      // The editor view may already be destroyed when flushing on unmount.
      return;
    }

    const found = await findUndismissedCredentials(
      text,
      getDismissedFingerprints(document.id)
    );
    if (scanId !== scanIdRef.current) {
      return;
    }

    const shown = shownRef.current;
    if (found.size === 0) {
      if (shown.size > 0) {
        // The flagged credentials were removed, so the warning is obsolete.
        // Programmatic dismissal does not fire onDismiss, so nothing is saved.
        toast.dismiss(toastId);
        shownRef.current = new Set();
      }
      return;
    }

    const unchanged =
      found.size === shown.size && [...found.keys()].every((fp) => shown.has(fp));
    if (unchanged) {
      return;
    }

    const fingerprints = [...found.keys()];
    shownRef.current = new Set(fingerprints);

    const dismiss = () => {
      addDismissedFingerprints(document.id, fingerprints);
      shownRef.current = new Set();
    };

    toast.warning(t("Possible credential detected"), {
      id: toastId,
      description: t(
        "“{{ documentTitle }}” may contain: {{ credentialTypes }}. Anyone with access to the document can see it, consider removing it.",
        {
          documentTitle: document.titleWithDefault,
          credentialTypes: [...new Set(found.values())].join(", "),
          interpolation: { escapeValue: false },
        }
      ),
      duration: Infinity,
      action: { label: t("Dismiss"), onClick: dismiss },
      onDismiss: dismiss,
    });
  }, [document, editorRef, t, toastId]);

  const scanRef = useRef(scan);
  useEffect(() => {
    scanRef.current = scan;
  });

  const debouncedScan = useMemo(
    () => debounce(() => void scanRef.current(), SCAN_DELAY),
    []
  );

  const flush = useCallback(() => {
    debouncedScan.cancel();
    if (pendingRef.current) {
      void scanRef.current();
    }
  }, [debouncedScan]);

  const handleChange = useCallback(
    (_value: unknown, event?: { remote: boolean }) => {
      if (!enabled || event?.remote) {
        return;
      }
      pendingRef.current = true;
      debouncedScan();
    },
    [enabled, debouncedScan]
  );

  // Scan pending edits when the user stops editing (e.g. "Done editing").
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!enabled) {
      flush();
    }
  }, [enabled, flush]);

  // Scan pending edits when leaving the document.
  useEffect(() => () => flush(), [flush]);

  return { handleChange, flush };
}
```

```typescript
import Storage from "@shared/utils/Storage";
import {
  addDismissedFingerprints,
  findUndismissedCredentials,
  fingerprintCredential,
  getDismissedFingerprints,
} from "./useCredentialScan";

const awsKey1 = `AKIA${"A".repeat(16)}`;
const awsKey2 = `AKIA${"B".repeat(16)}`;
const ghToken = `ghp_${"a1".repeat(18)}`;

describe("fingerprintCredential", () => {
  it("is stable for the same value", async () => {
    expect(await fingerprintCredential(awsKey1)).toEqual(
      await fingerprintCredential(awsKey1)
    );
  });

  it("differs for different values", async () => {
    expect(await fingerprintCredential(awsKey1)).not.toEqual(
      await fingerprintCredential(awsKey2)
    );
  });

  it("does not contain the credential itself", async () => {
    const fp = await fingerprintCredential(awsKey1);
    expect(fp).not.toContain(awsKey1);
    expect(fp).toMatch(/^[0-9a-f]{64}$/);
  });
});

describe("dismissed fingerprint storage", () => {
  const documentId = "doc-1";

  beforeEach(() => {
    Storage.remove(`credential-scan-dismissed:${documentId}`);
    Storage.remove("credential-scan-dismissed:doc-2");
  });

  it("returns an empty set when nothing is stored", () => {
    expect(getDismissedFingerprints(documentId).size).toBe(0);
  });

  it("round trips and merges fingerprints", () => {
    addDismissedFingerprints(documentId, ["a", "b"]);
    addDismissedFingerprints(documentId, ["b", "c"]);
    expect([...getDismissedFingerprints(documentId)].sort()).toEqual([
      "a",
      "b",
      "c",
    ]);
  });

  it("keeps dismissals separate per document", () => {
    addDismissedFingerprints(documentId, ["a"]);
    expect(getDismissedFingerprints("doc-2").size).toBe(0);
  });

  it("ignores malformed stored values", () => {
    Storage.set(`credential-scan-dismissed:${documentId}`, { not: "array" });
    expect(getDismissedFingerprints(documentId).size).toBe(0);
  });

  it("caps the number of stored fingerprints, keeping the newest", () => {
    addDismissedFingerprints(
      documentId,
      Array.from({ length: 250 }, (_, i) => `fp-${i}`)
    );
    const stored = getDismissedFingerprints(documentId);
    expect(stored.size).toBe(200);
    expect(stored.has("fp-249")).toBe(true);
    expect(stored.has("fp-0")).toBe(false);
  });
});

describe("findUndismissedCredentials", () => {
  it("returns nothing for clean text", async () => {
    const found = await findUndismissedCredentials("hello world", new Set());
    expect(found.size).toBe(0);
  });

  it("reports each distinct credential with its type", async () => {
    const found = await findUndismissedCredentials(
      `${awsKey1}\n${ghToken}`,
      new Set()
    );
    expect([...found.values()].sort()).toEqual([
      "AWS Access Key ID",
      "GitHub Token",
    ]);
  });

  it("reports the same credential once even if repeated", async () => {
    const found = await findUndismissedCredentials(
      `${awsKey1} and again ${awsKey1}`,
      new Set()
    );
    expect(found.size).toBe(1);
  });

  it("skips dismissed credentials but still reports new ones of the same type", async () => {
    const dismissed = new Set([await fingerprintCredential(awsKey1)]);
    const found = await findUndismissedCredentials(
      `${awsKey1}\n${awsKey2}`,
      dismissed
    );
    expect([...found.keys()]).toEqual([await fingerprintCredential(awsKey2)]);
    expect([...found.values()]).toEqual(["AWS Access Key ID"]);
  });
});
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-11-16 18:26:31Z)**_

I've built the client-side scanner and connected it to the document editor. It [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]es tests, the type check, and lint, but I haven't run it in a browser yet and nothing is committed.

**How it works** (the logic is in [useCredentialScan.ts](app/scenes/Document/hooks/useCredentialScan.ts)):
- **When it scans:** 2 seconds after your own edits stop. Edits that arrive from collaborators don't trigger a scan.
- **Saves and leaving:** clicking "Save draft" or "Done editing", publishing, blurring the title, or leaving the document runs any scan still waiting on that 2-second delay.
- **The warning:** a toast that stays up until closed, saying `"<doc title>" may contain: AWS Access Key ID, …`. It includes the document title because it can appear after you've already left the page.
- **Open question from the issue:** the warning shows only the credential type, never the matched text.
- **Dismissing:** the toast's "Dismiss" button, its close button, or swiping it away all count as a dismissal. Only fingerprints of the dismissed values are stored, per document, in this browser. They're SHA-256 hashes, with a fallback hash on non-HTTPS pages. Pasting a *different* key of the same type still warns.
- **If you delete the flagged credential:** the warning disappears on its own, and that doesn't count as a dismissal.
- **Saving is never blocked**, and nothing is sent to the server.

**Other changes:**
- [Editor.tsx](app/scenes/Document/components/Editor.tsx) now combines its existing change handler with the new one. Passing `onChange` straight through would have silently replaced the existing heading and task tracking.
- [Document.tsx](app/scenes/Document/components/Document.tsx) creates the scanner and routes the save actions through it.
- The two new strings are added to [translation.json](shared/i18n/locales/en_US/translation.json) by hand. The extractor script crashes on this machine because some of the script shortcuts in `node_modules/.bin` are broken, which also stopped `npx vitest` and `npx eslint` from running. Running `yarn install` would probably fix that.

**Verification:** the 12 new tests in [useCredentialScan.test.ts](app/scenes/Document/hooks/useCredentialScan.test.ts) [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri], along with the 54 credential-pattern tests. The full `tsc` run has 0 errors, and oxlint and oxfmt [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri] on the changed files.

**I was wrong earlier:** I said the local trigger avoids reacting to other people's edits. It doesn't on its own, because collaborators' changes also come through the local editor's `onChange`. It works only because the editor marks those edits as `remote` and the hook skips them.

**Limitations to know about:**
- The scan covers the whole document. If a co-author's key is already in the doc and you start typing, you'll be warned about it too.
- Dismissals live in this browser's local storage, so another device or browser will warn again.
- Document titles aren't scanned.
- A credential that was already in a document before this feature isn't flagged until someone edits the document, which matches "retroactive scanning" being out of scope.

Next you need to try it in the app: paste an AWS-style key, wait for the toast, dismiss it, edit again, and confirm there's no second warning. Do you want me to launch the app and walk through that, or commit first?

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-11-16 18:29:08Z)**_

Here's what should happen when you test it, based on how the code works. Use AWS's documented example key, `AKIA[REDACTED-AWS-SAMPLE-KEY]`. It matches the "AWS Access Key ID" pattern and isn't a real credential.

**Basic flow**

| You do | Expected |
|---|---|
| Paste `AKIA[REDACTED-AWS-SAMPLE-KEY]` into a doc you're editing, then stop typing | About 2 s later, a warning toast appears with the title **"Possible credential detected"** and the text *"“<doc title>” may contain: AWS Access Key ID. Anyone with access to the document can see it, consider removing it."*, plus a **Dismiss** button. It stays until you act on it. |
| Keep typing elsewhere in the doc | The same toast stays up. No duplicate or flashing toast. |
| Delete the key before dismissing | The toast disappears about 2 s after you stop typing. |
| Paste the same key again | You're warned again, because removing it isn't a dismissal. |
| Click **Dismiss** (or swipe the toast away) | The toast closes. The document is saved as normal; saving was never blocked. |
| Keep editing with the dismissed key still in the doc | No new warning. |
| Reload the page and edit again | Still no warning, because the dismissal is remembered for this doc in this browser. |

**Several credentials**

| You do | Expected |
|---|---|
| Paste a *different* AWS key, e.g. `AKIA[REDACTED-AWS-SAMPLE-KEY]` | A new warning. Dismissing the first key doesn't cover this one. |
| Have an AWS key and a GitHub token (`ghp_` followed by 36 letters/digits) in the doc, neither dismissed | One toast listing **"AWS Access Key ID, GitHub Token"**. If the same key appears twice in the text, it's listed once. |
| Add a second key while a toast is already showing | The existing toast updates to list both. Dismiss then covers both. |

**Timing and backstops**

| You do | Expected |
|---|---|
| Paste a key and click "Save draft", "Done editing", or publish within 2 s | The warning appears right away and the save goes through normally. |
| Paste a key and navigate to another page within 2 s | The warning appears on the page you navigated to. That's why it names the document. |
| Open a doc that already contains a key and don't edit it | No warning. Scanning existing documents is out of scope. Your first edit scans the whole doc, so a warning would appear then. |

**Who gets warned**

| Situation | Expected |
|---|---|
| Viewing a doc in read-only mode, revision history, or a public share link | No scanning and no warning. |
| A collaborator pastes a key while you both have the doc open | Their browser warns them. Yours doesn't, until *you* make an edit. Then you're warned too, because your scan covers the whole document. |
| Same doc in another browser or device after you dismissed | Warns again, because dismissals are stored per browser. |

**Privacy check:** in the browser's DevTools, the Network tab should show no request containing the key apart from Outline's normal document syncing, and nothing about the scan or the warning. The Application → Local Storage tab should show a key `credential-scan-dismissed:<documentId>` holding 64-character hex hashes, never the key text.

**What depends on settings:** the **"Done editing"** button only exists if the user has the separate edit mode setting turned on. With the default seamless editing, there's no such button. The 2 s scan and the scan on leaving the document cover that case.

I can launch the app and go through these myself if you'd like. Otherwise, these rows work as a manual test checklist for the PR.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-11-16 19:14:17Z)**_

We picked the trigger by working through five options in turn. Each one we dropped had a specific problem, and the last one we tried avoided all of them.

## What the trigger had to do

From the acceptance criteria and the code:
- **Scan on the client**, so nothing sensitive is sent anywhere.
- **Warn without blocking** the save.
- **Fire when the user is actually editing.** In the multiplayer editor, which nearly every document opens in, body text is sent to the server as you type. There's no single "save" moment.
- **Show up while the author can still act on it.**

## The alternatives

**1. The "Save draft" / "Done editing" buttons only.** This was the issue's original wording ("hits save"). You pointed out the problem: people rarely click those buttons. With the default editing mode, "Done editing" doesn't even exist. Most authors would never see the warning.

**2. When the user leaves the document.** You suggested this as a way to catch people who never click the buttons. It doesn't work well:
- Closing the tab or browser only gets the browser's generic "Leave site?" dialog. You can't say which credential was found, and browsers often skip it.
- Navigating within the app would need a prompt that stops the user until they respond, which goes against "warns but doesn't prevent".
- It's the latest possible moment. The key has been stored on the server since it was pasted.

We kept "on leave" as a backstop, not as the main trigger.

**3. The existing autosave in `useDocumentSave`.** This was your original idea, which you'd set aside because you thought it would be too expensive. Two findings:
- **Cost wasn't the problem.** Scanning takes about 0.04 ms on a 10 KB document and about 3–5 ms on 1 MB, including text built to slow the patterns down.
- **The real problem:** that 3-second autosave only runs when the *title* changes. In the multiplayer editor, body edits sync through the collaboration server and never call it. Hooking into autosave would have missed pasted keys entirely.

**4. Watching the `lastEditedAt` field.** You suggested this. The server sets it whenever it saves an edit, and the browser hears about it through a `documents.update` websocket event. It does match "on update" literally. But:
- **It fires for everyone's edits.** Every viewer receives the event, so a co-author's paste would warn you. Filtering by `lastModifiedById` is unreliable when several people edit at once, because it only records whoever's change triggered the save.
- **It's only a timing signal.** The event doesn't include the content, so we'd scan the local editor anyway. It just arrives later.
- **More can go wrong:** it depends on the server delay, the event queue, and a live websocket. If the socket drops, there's no warning.
- **It belongs to another feature.** The field exists for stale-document detection, and changing it for that reason could quietly break scanning.

**5. Scanning on the server.** This was never really an option. The acceptance criteria require scanning on the client, so sensitive content doesn't end up in server-side handling or logs.

## What we chose: a debounced local editor-change scan

The editor already reports every content change through `onChange`. The hook:
- **waits 2 s after the user's own edits stop**, then scans the editor's plain text, so it isn't scanning on every keystroke;
- **skips collaborators' edits.** I got this wrong at first: I said the local trigger avoids other people's edits by design. It doesn't, because remote edits also come through the local editor's `onChange`. What makes it work is that the editor marks those edits as `remote`, and the hook ignores them;
- **runs any waiting scan on saves and on leaving** (button, publish, title blur, leaving the document) as backstops;
- **takes about 2 s** to warn, while the author is still in the document and can delete the key.

It covers what each alternative was reaching for:
- It runs in both editing modes (multiplayer or not).
- It needs no server round trip and keeps working when the websocket is disconnected.
- It reuses no field meant for another feature.
- It never blocks the user.

## What it doesn't change

- **The key still reaches the server.** The multiplayer editor syncs content as it's typed, so a warning can prompt removal but can't prevent storage. The user story's "before it sits exposed" overstates this, and the issue or PR should say so.
- **The scan covers the whole document.** Once you edit, you'll be warned about a co-author's key that's in the doc too.

## Design decision: What happens when review and edit happen at the same time

The server doesn't coordinate review actions with edits. There's no version check and no locking on the review side. When a review action and an edit happen at about the same time, whichever save reaches the database last decides the review status. I went with the last save being what “wins” mostly because it gives the right answer in the case that matters most, and it cost nothing to build. It started as the default behaviour of the existing code. An approval only ever writes the review status, never the content, so no edit can be lost. Any edit saved after an approval moves the document back to draft, so unreviewed content never shows as approved. 

Adding coordination would also have meant more locking around a document row that the live editor already locks every few seconds, and time this sprint was better spent on the UI. The first alternative is to lock the document row in the three review routes, about one line each. Simultaneous review actions would then run one after another, which would stop history from recording the wrong previous reviewer or two decisions at once. The cost is a short wait when an edit is saving at the same moment. 

The second alternative is to have the reviewer approve a specific version. The app would send the revision the reviewer was reading, and the server would reject the approval if the content had changed since. That would make "approved" mean "this exact version was reviewed", which closes the remaining weakness of approving text the reviewer never saw. The cost is a new API field, extra client work and another error for users to handle, so it fits better as future work than in this sprint.

## New files:

**app/components/RequestReviewDialog.tsx (162 lines)**
The reviewer picker, opened from Request review in the document menu.
- A searchable list of active members. It leaves out the current user, suspended users and people who haven't joined yet.
- The current reviewer is pre-selected. The submit button says Request review, Change reviewer or Request review again, depending on the situation.
- Submit is disabled until someone is chosen, and while the request is saving.
- Problems with the chosen reviewer show inside the dialog. "Share this document with the reviewer first" also gets a Share document link. Any other error shows as a toast.

**app/scenes/Document/components/ReviewStatusBadge.tsx (147 lines)**
The status badge in the document header:
- Needs review, with the tooltip "Previously approved by {reviewer}".
- In review · {reviewer}, with "Review requested by {requester}". It shows "Reviewer unavailable" if the reviewer's account was deleted.
- Changes requested, in yellow, with "Changes requested by {reviewer}".
- Approved, highlighted, with "Approved by {reviewer}".

The labels and tooltips live in a plain function, `reviewStatusDisplay`, so they can be tested without rendering. "Needs review" is used for `draft` because Outline already shows a "Draft" badge for unpublished documents.

## Modified files: server code (2)

**server/models/Document.ts (+19)**
Adds `reviewStatusAfterEdit`: approved becomes draft, and every other status stays the same. The existing save hook calls it whenever content, text or title changes.

**server/commands/documentCollaborativeUpdater.ts (+2)**
Applies the same rule when saving live edits, since this path runs with hooks turned off.

## Modified files: app code (10)

**app/actions/definitions/documents.tsx (+134)**
Adds four actions:
- `requestDocumentReview` opens the picker. It's labelled Request review…, Change reviewer… or Request review again….
- `requestDocumentReviewAgain` sends the document straight back to the same reviewer. It's offered when a document is Changes requested or Needs review, and never to the reviewer, who can't review their own request.
- `approveDocument` and `requestDocumentChanges` are offered only to the assigned reviewer, using the server's `review` permission.

All four check permissions the server sends, so the buttons follow the Part 1 rules without repeating them.

**app/hooks/useDocumentMenuAction.tsx (+6)**
Adds the new actions to the document menu, next to Mark as not stale.

**app/scenes/Document/components/Header.tsx (+46)**
- Shows the badge in the header's actions area. The title area only appears after scrolling, so a badge there was hidden at the top of a document.
- Adds Approve and Request changes buttons for the reviewer, and a Request review again button for the author.
- Buttons disable themselves while their request runs.

**app/models/Document.ts (+58)**
- Adds `reviewStatus`, `reviewerId` and `reviewRequestedById` to the app's document model.
- `visibleReviewStatus` returns null whenever the workflow is off, so nothing shows even if old data is cached.
- `canRequestReviewAgain` decides when to offer Request review again.
- Adds `requestReview`, `approve` and `requestChanges`.

**app/stores/DocumentsStore.ts (+43)**
Adds the three review calls. Each updates the document and its permissions from the server's response, the same way the existing review (mark as not stale) call does.

**app/stores/UsersStore.ts (+15)**
Adds `reviewCandidates`, the list the picker shows.

**app/scenes/Settings/Security.tsx (+24)**
Adds a Review workflow switch under Settings → Security → Behavior. Only admins can open this page. A failed save shows an error and the switch flips back.

## Bug fixes and renames outside this feature

**shared/constants.ts (+2)**
Gives the staleness threshold a default of 180 days. Without a saved value, the app's settings lookup returned `false`, which caused two bugs in the stale-document feature:
- the badge read "Not edited in the last false days";
- every published document counted as stale, so Mark as reviewed appeared to do nothing.

**app/actions/definitions/documents.tsx, app/components/DocumentMeta.tsx, app/scenes/Document/components/History/EventListItem.tsx (1–2 lines each)**
Renames "Mark as reviewed" to "Mark as not stale", along with its toast, its history entry and the line under the title. Having both "Mark as reviewed" and the review workflow was confusing. Only the wording changed, not the endpoint or the stored fields.

**shared/i18n/locales/en_US/translation.json (+28, −5)**
New strings for all of the above, with the renamed and unused ones removed.

7 tests:
- Editing the text or title of an approved document moves it to draft.
- Changing full width keeps the approval.
- Draft, In review, Changes requested and no status are unchanged by an edit.

**server/commands/documentCollaborativeUpdater.test.ts (+71)**

## Moved to Part 3

These are saved on the `review-workflow-part3-parked` branch:
- **The warning before editing an approved document.** It can be by[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]ed until live updates exist, so it belongs with them.

- **A friendly message when an approval is refused.** For now, a stale Approve click shows the server's own error.

## Tech Debt (besides the design decision already mentioned)

**Introduced:**

**The status doesn't update live for other users**
What: Other people's screens only show a status change after a reload. That includes the editor's own badge after an edit moves the document to Needs review.
Why: The Part 1 debt below. Live update messages are built without a logged-in user, so the review fields are left out, and the app keeps the old values.
When to fix: Part 3, by including the review fields in those messages.

**The picker recognises the no-access error by its text**
What: The picker checks for the exact message "Share this document with the reviewer first" to decide whether to show the Share link.
Why: The server sends a plain 400 with no error code.
When to fix: When the server error gets a code. Until then, changing that message on the server quietly removes the link.

**Encountered:**

**Review fields only show up when the logged-in user's workspace is available (from Part 1)**
This is now visible in the app, as the "doesn't update live" problem above.

**Review actions increase the revision count**
Requesting, approving and requesting changes all count as a revision, because the check for review-only saves only covers the stale feature's fields. Not fixed here. It's a one-line fix planned for the next PR.

```markdown
## Design decision: When the scan runs

The scan runs in the browser 2 seconds after the author stops typing. It reacts only to the author's own edits. Edits that come in from collaborators are ignored. Any scan still waiting also runs when the author clicks Save draft, Done editing or Publish, blurs the title, or leaves the document. I went with this because it's the only trigger that fires for every edit in both editing modes, without a round trip to the server and without blocking the author. It also warns while the author is still in the document and can delete the key.

The issue's wording ("hits save") points to the Save draft / Done editing buttons, but people rarely click them, and with the default editing mode Done editing doesn't exist. Most authors would never see the warning, so the buttons are only a backstop here.

The first alternative was to warn when the author leaves the document. Closing the tab can only show the browser's generic "Leave site?" dialog, which can't say what was found, and browsers often skip it. Navigating inside the app would need a prompt that stops the author until they answer, which goes against "warns but does not prevent". It's also the latest possible moment, so leaving is kept only as a backstop.

The second alternative was the existing 3-second autosave in `useDocumentSave`. In the multiplayer editor, body text syncs through the collaboration server and never calls that autosave. Only title changes do. A pasted key would never be scanned. Performance wasn't the reason against it: a scan takes about 0.04 ms on a 10 KB document and 3–5 ms on 1 MB, including text built to slow the patterns down.

The third alternative was to watch `lastEditedAt`, which the server sets when it saves an edit and sends to every open copy of the document. That fires for everyone's edits, so a co-author's paste would warn you too. The message doesn't carry the content, so we'd still scan the local editor, just later. It also relies on a live websocket and on a field that belongs to the stale-document feature.

Scanning on the server was ruled out by the acceptance criteria, which require scanning in the browser so the content never reaches a logging endpoint.

Collaborators' edits also reach the local editor's change handler. The editor already marks them as remote, so the hook skips them.

This doesn't stop the key from reaching the server. The multiplayer editor syncs content as it's typed, so the warning can prompt the author to remove a key but can't prevent it being stored. The user story's "before it sits exposed" overstates this.

## New files:

**app/scenes/Document/hooks/useCredentialScan.ts (265 lines)**
The hook that scans the editor and shows the warning.
- It waits 2 seconds after the author's own edits stop, then scans the editor's plain text. It skips edits from collaborators.
- `flush` runs any waiting scan right away. It's called on saves, when the author stops editing, and when the document closes. The close uses a layout effect, because a normal effect runs after React has already cleared the editor ref, so it couldn't read the text.
- The warning is a toast, "Possible credential detected", that names the document and the credential types, e.g. "AWS Access Key ID, GitHub Token". It stays until the author dismisses it. It never shows the matched text, which answers the issue's open question.
- If a newly found credential appears while the toast is up, it updates to list it. If the author deletes the flagged credentials, it closes on its own, and that doesn't count as a dismissal.
- Dismissing (Dismiss button, close button or swipe) remembers the dismissed values for that document in local storage, as SHA-256 fingerprints and never as raw text. Only those exact values are skipped, so a different key of the same type still warns. Pages served without HTTPS fall back to a fast non-cryptographic hash, which is fine here because it's only used to avoid repeat warnings.
- The helper functions (`fingerprintCredential`, `getDismissedFingerprints`, `addDismissedFingerprints`, `findUndismissedCredentials`) are exported so they can be tested without rendering.

## Modified files: shared code (2)

**shared/utils/credentialPatterns.ts (+38, −1)**
Adds `findCredentialMatches`, which returns every match with its pattern name, the matched text and its position. `scanForCredentials` only returns pattern names, and only one per pattern, so it couldn't tell two different AWS keys apart, which the "don't re-warn for the same credential" criterion needs. It works on global copies of the patterns, so the shared, non-global patterns are left unchanged. The existing patterns and `scanForCredentials` are unchanged.

**shared/i18n/locales/en_US/translation.json (+2)**
The toast's title and description. I added them by hand because the extractor script fails on my Windows setup, so running `yarn build:i18n` may reorder them.

## Modified files: app code (2)

**app/scenes/Document/components/Editor.tsx (+10, −1)**
Combines the existing change handler, which updates headings and tasks, with an optional `onChange` from the parent. Passing `onChange` straight through would have silently replaced the existing handler, because `{...rest}` is spread after it.

**app/scenes/Document/components/Document.tsx (+25, −4)**
- Sets up the hook. Scanning is on only when the document isn't read-only and the user can update it.
- Adds `onSaveAndScan`, which runs any waiting scan and then calls `onSave`. The header, the editor and the publish action use it.

## Test files:

**shared/utils/credentialPatterns.test.ts (+60, −4)**
6 new tests for `findCredentialMatches`:
- Clean text returns nothing.
- It returns the name, matched text and position.
- Repeated keys of the same type are each reported.
- Matches from different patterns are ordered by position.
- It finds the same pattern names as `scanForCredentials`.
- The shared patterns are left unchanged.

**app/scenes/Document/hooks/useCredentialScan.test.ts (111 lines)**
12 tests:
- Fingerprints are stable, differ for different values and don't contain the credential.
- Dismissals round-trip and merge, stay separate per document, ignore bad stored data and keep only the newest 200.
- Each distinct credential is reported once with its type, and dismissing one key doesn't hide a different key of the same type.

All 54 credential pattern tests and the 14 tests in the document hooks folder [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]. The type check and lint [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri].

Manually tested in the browser: [fill in, e.g. pasted a fake key of each of the 12 types, saw the warning after about 2 seconds, dismissed it and saw no new warning after editing or reloading, pasted a different key of the same type and was warned again, deleted a flagged key and saw the warning close, clicked Done editing and left the page right after pasting and still got the warning, and saw none of the false-positive examples trigger].

## Out of scope

As listed in the issue:
- **Scanning existing documents.** A key already in a document isn't flagged until someone edits it. The first edit then scans the whole document.
- **Notifying admins.** Separate issue.
- **Redacting or masking keys automatically.**

## Tech Debt (besides the design decision already mentioned)

**Introduced:**

**Dismissals are per browser**
What: A dismissed warning comes back on another browser or device, or after site data is cleared.
Why: Storing dismissals on the server would mean sending credential fingerprints there, which goes against keeping scanning in the browser.
When to fix: Only if people complain. A server-side list of fingerprints per user and document would work, but it needs a decision on whether storing fingerprints there is acceptable.

**The scan covers the whole document, not just your own edits**
What: Once you edit, you're also warned about a key a co-author pasted, which their browser already warned them about.
Why: Working out which text you personally added in a multiplayer document is much harder than scanning the whole text, and the warning is still accurate.
When to fix: Probably never. Arguably anyone editing should know.

**Document titles aren't scanned**
What: A key typed into the title isn't caught.
Why: Title changes don't go through the editor's change handler.
When to fix: Next PR. It's small: also schedule a scan from `handleChangeTitle`.

**Encountered:**

**The pattern library only reported pattern names**
`scanForCredentials` used `.test()`, so it couldn't return the matched text or more than one hit per pattern. Fixed here with `findCredentialMatches`. `scanForCredentials` is kept as it was, though nothing uses it yet.

Closes #[issue number]
```

```bash
credential is not warned about again. Saving is never blocked.

not just pattern names, can be told apart.
```
